mainTopic: Opening locks across domains on שבת: רבי מאיר vs. the חכמים, חוקקין להשלים, רב דימי's rule on a מקום פטור, and a new משנה on a knobbed bolt
overview: This amud finishes a משנה where רבי מאיר says a person may not stand in one domain and open a lock in another domain unless he builds a ten-טפחים מחיצה. The חכמים answer with a story about a market in ירושלים where merchants took the key from a window above the door, and רבי יוסי corrects which market it was. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא about garden gates and shop locks, where רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about where the key may be kept when the lock is high. The גמרא asks how big that lock is. אביי answers that it is under four by four but could be carved out to four, and the two sides argue whether we count that carving room (חוקקין להשלים). רב ביבי בר אביי draws three lessons from this. First, the rule of חוקקין להשלים has a source. Second, רבי מאיר retracted his strict ruling in the משנה. Third, the חכמים support רב דימי's rule that a מקום פטור may not be used to pass objects between two restricted domains. A new משנה follows, in which רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי argue about locking with a knobbed bolt and each tells the טבריה story in the opposite way. The גמרא begins narrowing their dispute, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר requires a ten-handbreadth partition
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה: רבי מאיר rules that one may not use the key unless he builds a מחיצה ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Unless he built a partition ten handbreadths high — these are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the משנה's rule that a person may not stand in one domain (for example the רשות הרבים) and open a lock that is in the other domain (the רשות היחיד), or the reverse. רבי מאיר says this is forbidden unless he first builds a ten-טפחים מחיצה around where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that while opening, he will move the key, or the lock, from one domain into the other. A ten-טפחים מחיצה turns the spot where he stands into an enclosed private area, so he and the lock are no longer in different domains. This is a strict view, and the חכמים push back on it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי מאיר (attribution formula)

phrases.english: unless he made a partition
phrases.notes: Continues the משנה from the previous daf

phrases.english: ten handbreadths high,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשָׂה מְחִיצָה גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's ruling begun in the משנה on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not stand in one domain and open a lock in another domain unless he builds a ten-טפחים מחיצה (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The Rabbis cite the poultry market in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים prove from a real event in ירושלים that people kept keys in the window above the door without any מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There was an incident at the poultry dealers' market in ירושלים, where they would lock their doors and place the key in the window above the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue against רבי מאיר by telling a story. In a market in ירושלים, people locked their shops and left the key in the window over the door, apparently with no מחיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof from practice (מעשה): the people of ירושלים openly did this, so it must be allowed. They stood in the street and took the key from the window above the door to open their shops, without building any מחיצה. This challenges רבי מאיר's requirement of a ten-טפחים מחיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him (the חכמים answering רבי מאיר)
An incident, a real event used as proof

phrases.english: They said to him: There was an incident
phrases.notes: The חכמים respond to רבי מאיר

phrases.english: at the market of the poultry dealers
that was in Jerusalem,
where they would lock and place the key
in the window that was above the doorway.
phrases.notes: The window was higher than ten טפחים

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשׁוּק שֶׁל פַּטָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.raayaObject: That the key may be used from the high window without a מחיצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The established practice at a market in ירושלים

steps.title: רבי יוסי corrects the name of the market
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the market in the story was the wool dealers' market, not the poultry market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It was the wool dealers' market.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי accepts the story but corrects one detail: which market it was. In his version, it was the market of the wool sellers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not change the law the חכמים were proving. It only corrects the historical record of where the event took place.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not arguing about the הלכה here. He is only correcting which market the story happened in.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It was a market of wool dealers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שׁוּק שֶׁל צַמָּרִים הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects a factual detail in the חכמים' story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incident took place in the wool dealers' market.

steps.title: Garden gates may be opened from the side with a gatehouse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: garden gates may be opened and locked from whichever side has a בית שער, and if there is no gatehouse on either side, it is forbidden on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Garden gates — when they have a gatehouse on the inside, one opens and locks from inside. If the gatehouse is outside, one opens and locks from outside. If there is one on both sides, one opens and locks from both sides. If there is none on either side, it is forbidden on both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with practical rules for opening a garden gate on שבת. Everything depends on where a בית שער (gatehouse) stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gatehouse is a private domain, and so is the lock area, so the key may move between them. Without a gatehouse on a given side, you would be bringing the key from the רשות הרבים or from the garden (a כרמלית) into the lock, which is not allowed. So the side with a gatehouse is the side you may open from.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: The entrances of garden gates,

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁעַר מִבִּפְנִים —
phrases.english: when they have a gatehouse on the inside —
one opens and locks from inside,
on the outside — one opens and locks from outside,
on this side and that side —
one opens and locks here and there.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן לֹא לְכָאן וְלֹא לְכָאן —
phrases.english: if they have none, neither here nor there —
they are forbidden here and there.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פִּתְחֵי שַׁעֲרֵי גִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the related topic of opening locks on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garden gate may be opened and locked only from a side that has a בית שער.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the location of the person and the key, measured in domains, decides whether opening a lock on שבת is allowed.

steps.title: Shops with a low lock: keep the key on the threshold
steps.stepSummary: Shops opening to the רשות הרבים with a lock below ten טפחים: put the key on the threshold before שבת, then open, lock, and return it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, shops that open to the public domain: when the lock is below ten handbreadths, one brings the key before שבת and places it on the threshold. The next day he opens and locks and puts it back on the threshold.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second case: shop doors facing the רשות הרבים. When the lock is low, the key is left on the threshold (איסקופה) from ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lock below ten טפחים counts as part of the רשות הרבים. The threshold has the status of a כרמלית, so the key stays in a nearby, separate spot. He uses it on שבת and returns it to the same threshold.

phrases.english: And likewise, shops that open into the public domain,
when the lock is below ten handbreadths —
one brings a key from Shabbat eve
and places it on the threshold,
the next day he opens and locks
and returns it to the threshold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן חֲנוּיוֹת הַפְּתוּחוֹת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel case (וכן)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a lock below ten טפחים, the key is kept on the threshold and returned there after use.

steps.title: Shops with a high lock: keep the key in the lock
steps.stepSummary: When the lock is above ten טפחים, put the key in the lock before שבת, then open, lock, and return it to its place. The ברייתא attributes this to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the lock is above ten handbreadths, one brings the key before שבת and places it in the lock. The next day he opens and locks and returns it to its place — these are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the last case: a high lock. The key is left in the lock area itself and put back there after use. The ruling is credited to רבי מאיר, which sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lock above ten טפחים is treated as a separate private area, so the key stays inside that same area the whole time. Notice that רבי מאיר is lenient here, even though in the משנה he was strict and demanded a מחיצה. This apparent contrast is what the coming discussion will need to explain.
steps.whatToRemember: Garden gates: open from the side with a בית שער. Shops with a low lock: keep the key on the threshold. Shops with a high lock: keep the key in the lock. The last ruling is רבי מאיר's.

phrases.english: And when the lock is above ten handbreadths —
one brings a key from Shabbat eve
and places it in the lock,
the next day he opens and locks
and returns it to its place,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Naming רבי מאיר here sets up the question the גמרא is about to ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהַמַּנְעוּל לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with the contrasting case of a high lock
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a lock above ten טפחים, the key is kept in the lock and returned there (רבי מאיר).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי מאיר is lenient here but strict in the משנה. That contrast drives the next part of the סוגיא.

steps.title: The Sages allow the key on the threshold even for a high lock
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that even when the lock is above ten טפחים, the key may be left on the threshold or in the window above the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: even when the lock is higher than ten handbreadths, a person brings the key before שבת and puts it on the threshold. The next day he opens and locks the door, then puts the key back in its place, or in the window above the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opinion of the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר from the previous step about a lock that is high up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר required the key to be left inside the high lock itself. The חכמים say the key may stay on the threshold, just as with a low lock. They also allow keeping it in the window above the door.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion arguing with רבי מאיר
Even when (extends the ruling to a further case)

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Even when the lock
is above ten handbreadths,
he brings a key on Shabbat eve,
and places it on the threshold;
the next day he opens and locks
phrases.notes: He takes the key from the threshold and uses it in the lock.

phrases.english: and returns it to its place,
or in the window that is above the doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַמַּנְעוּל לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a lock above ten טפחים, the key may be kept on the threshold or in the window above the door.

steps.title: A large window may not be used
steps.stepSummary: If the window measures four by four טפחים, it is forbidden to put the key there, because that is like moving it from one domain to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the window is four by four handbreadths, it is forbidden, because it is like carrying from one domain to another domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to the window option it just allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A window of four by four טפחים is big enough to count as its own רשות. Putting the key there from the threshold would mean moving it between two different domains, which is forbidden. A smaller window does not count as a separate domain, so it is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Window, here a niche above the door
Four by four handbreadths, the minimum size for an area to count as a domain
Domain, a halachic zone for carrying on שבת

phrases.english: If the window has
four by four handbreadths, it is forbidden,
because it is like one who carries out
from one domain to another domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ בַּחַלּוֹן אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the window option the חכמים allowed in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A window of four by four טפחים is a separate domain, so the key may not be placed there.

steps.title: The threshold must be a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'and similarly shops', the גמרא infers that the ברייתא is talking about a threshold that has the status of a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא said 'and similarly shops', we learn that we are dealing with a threshold that is a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts its own analysis by figuring out what kind of area the threshold is. This sets up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shops open onto the public street. Even so, the ברייתא lets you move the key from their threshold to the lock. That only makes sense if the threshold is a כרמלית, a rabbinic in-between zone, and not a true public domain. Once we know the threshold is a כרמלית, the גמרא can ask about the lock's status.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between domain, restricted only by the Rabbis

phrases.english: Since it says: 'And similarly shops,'
phrases.notes: Refers to the shops case in step 5.

phrases.english: we can infer that we are dealing with a threshold that is a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר: ״וְכֵן חֲנוּיוֹת״, מִכְּלָל דִּבְאִיסְקוּפַּת כַּרְמְלִית עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the ברייתא it has just finished quoting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The threshold in the ברייתא is a כרמלית.

steps.title: What kind of lock is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the lock's status is. If it is smaller than four by four, it is a מקום פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This lock, what is the case? If it is not four handbreadths wide, it is an exempt place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how big the lock is. It gives the first possibility and is setting up a challenge that will come from the second possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An area smaller than four by four טפחים is a מקום פטור, a place that belongs to no domain. Moving the key from a כרמלית into such a place is no problem, so this option fits the חכמים. But it leaves no reason for ר' מאיר to insist that the key stay in the lock rather than on the threshold. The second option, in the next step, creates the real problem for the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt area, belonging to no domain

phrases.english: This lock, what are its circumstances?
If it does not have four handbreadths,
it is an exempt place.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַנְעוּל הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the threshold being a כרמלית to ask about the lock
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the lock four by four טפחים (a domain) or smaller (a מקום פטור)?

steps.title: If the lock is a private domain, how can the Sages allow it?
steps.stepSummary: If the lock is four by four, it is a רשות היחיד. Then the חכמים would be allowing someone to move the key from a כרמלית to a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is four handbreadths, would the Rabbis really say in that case that even with a lock above ten, he puts the key on the threshold, opens and locks with it, and returns it to the threshold or window? But he is moving it from a כרמלית to a רשות היחיד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים using the second possibility: a lock big enough to count as a private domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lock that is four by four and above ten טפחים counts as a רשות היחיד. The threshold is a כרמלית, as we learned in step 9. Taking the key from the threshold to the lock would mean carrying between these domains, which the Rabbis forbid. So how could the חכמים allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: But look, the opening of a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the key is used on שבת. The problem is moving it between two different domains: from the כרמלית threshold to the private-domain lock.

phrases.english: And if it does have four handbreadths,
would the Rabbis say in this case:
Even when the lock is above ten,
he brings a key on Shabbat eve
and places it on the threshold;
the next day he opens and locks with it
and returns it to the threshold
or to the window above the doorway?
But he is moving it
from a karmelit to a private domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מְטַלְטֵל מִכַּרְמְלִית לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in step 10 with the problematic possibility
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the חכמים in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A four-by-four lock above ten טפחים is a רשות היחיד, and the threshold is a כרמלית. Moving the key between them should be forbidden, yet the חכמים allow it.

steps.title: אביי: The lock is small but can be carved out to four
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the challenge. The lock really is less than four by four טפחים, but there is enough room in the door around it to carve it out to a full four.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the lock is less than four by four. But there is room around it to carve out a hole and complete it to four.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the קשיא from Step 11 by saying the lock is small, under four by four. He adds one more detail: the door around it is wide enough to carve the space out to four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the lock is under four, the חכמים can treat it as a מקום פטור, and the challenge goes away. The extra detail about carving room is the setup for the next step, where ר' מאיר and the חכמים disagree about whether that potential space counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Used when the גמרא returns to a choice it had seemed to reject.
To carve out, to hollow out
To complete it (to the needed size)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the lock is four by four. It is physically smaller. The point is only that it could be carved out to four, and the next step asks whether that possibility counts.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Actually, it (the lock) is not four by four,
but there is room in it to carve out
and complete it to four.
phrases.notes: The wood of the door around the lock is wide enough to widen the hole to four by four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם דְּאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11 by choosing the 'less than four' option and adding a new detail about carving room.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the lock is small but could be carved out to four)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that if the חכמים allow the key in the lock, the lock must be a four-by-four רשות היחיד, which is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lock is under four, so for the חכמים it is a מקום פטור. The carving room explains why ר' מאיר treats it differently.

steps.title: The dispute: Do we carve out to complete four?
steps.stepSummary: ר' מאיר holds חוקקין להשלים: we view the space as if it were already carved out to four. The חכמים hold אין חוקקין להשלים: we look only at the actual size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about: רבי מאיר holds that we carve out to complete, and the Rabbis hold that we do not carve out to complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer by spelling out what ר' מאיר and the חכמים disagree about. The question is whether space that could be carved out counts as if it already were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ר' מאיר the lock counts as four by four, so it is a real domain (רשות היחיד). For the חכמים it stays its actual small size, so it is a מקום פטור. This explains why the two sides rule differently about the key.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what they argue about
We 'carve out to complete': a space that could be widened to four is treated as if it already were four
We do not 'carve out to complete': only the actual size counts

steps.whyThisMatters: חוקקין להשלים is a general rule in the laws of domains on שבת. It asks whether we judge a place by what it is now or by what it could easily become.

phrases.english: And in this they disagree:
that Rabbi Meir holds
we carve out to complete (the four).
phrases.notes: So for ר' מאיר the lock counts as four by four, a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
we do not carve out to complete.
phrases.notes: So for the חכמים the lock stays under four, a מקום פטור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהָא פְּלִיגִי: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר חוֹקְקִין לְהַשְׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by naming the underlying point of dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Locating the dispute in a general principle (חוקקין להשלים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the חכמים were allowing a transfer into a רשות היחיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים do not count the carving room, so for them the lock is only a מקום פטור. ר' מאיר does count it, so for him the lock is a full domain.

steps.title: First lesson: We carve out to complete
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי says this ברייתא teaches three lessons. The first is that the rule of חוקקין להשלים exists (according to ר' מאיר).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: Learn three things from this ברייתא. Learn from it that we carve out to complete.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that אביי has explained the ברייתא, his son רב ביבי draws practical lessons from it. He announces three lessons and gives the first one here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, חוקקין להשלים was only a reasonable idea. Now we have a source showing that a תנא (ר' מאיר) actually holds it. The phrase 'three things' sets up the next two lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / we can conclude from it
A teaching of the תנאים (here, the ברייתא)

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said,
learn from this baraita three things:
learn from it that we carve out to complete.
phrases.notes: First lesson, based on ר' מאיר's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מֵהָא מַתְנִיתָא תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's explanation and draws a halachic lesson from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is a source in the תנאים for the rule of חוקקין להשלים.

steps.title: Second lesson: רבי מאיר retracted about garden gates
steps.stepSummary: The second lesson is that ר' מאיר took back his earlier ruling about garden gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it that רבי מאיר retracted from (his view about) garden gates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי gives his second lesson: this ברייתא shows that ר' מאיר changed his mind about an earlier case involving garden gates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Garden gates' does not mean the anonymous ברייתא in step 4. It refers to ר' מאיר's ruling in the משנה (step 1), which רבא earlier explained as a case of garden gates. There, ר' מאיר forbids someone standing in a כרמלית to open a lock that is a רשות היחיד unless he builds a מחיצה. Here, ר' מאיר treats the lock as a רשות היחיד (because of חוקקין להשלים), yet he lets a person outside use it with no מחיצה. That shows he retracted his ruling in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Garden gates: the case of ר' מאיר's ruling in the משנה, as explained earlier by רבא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Retracted' does not mean the ברייתא contradicts ר' מאיר. It means this ruling is his later view, which replaces what he said about garden gates.

phrases.english: And learn from it
that Rabbi Meir retracted
from (his ruling about) garden gates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשַּׁעֲרֵי גִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of the three lessons announced in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ר' מאיר's final view permits this case, so his earlier stricter ruling about garden gates is set aside.

steps.title: Third lesson: The Rabbis support רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: The third lesson is that the חכמים' view supports רב דימי, who quoted ר' יוחנן: a place under four by four is a מקום פטור that people from either domain may use to adjust their load, but they may not pass objects to each other through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you learn from the Rabbis that רב דימי's ruling is correct. For when רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A place that is not four by four, it is permitted for people of the public domain and people of the private domain to adjust their loads on it, as long as they do not exchange (objects).
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי gives his third lesson: the חכמים' position backs up a ruling of רב דימי, which the גמרא now quotes in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's rule has two parts. People on both sides may rest or adjust things on a small exempt place, but they may not use it to pass objects from one restricted domain to the other. The חכמים likewise treat the lock as a מקום פטור, yet they still do not allow it to serve as a bridge between the threshold (a כרמלית) and the window (a רשות היחיד). That matches the 'no exchanging' condition.

keyTerms.meaning: רב דימי's ruling stands / is correct
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
To adjust a load on one's shoulder
As long as they do not exchange (objects with each other)

steps.whatToRemember: Three lessons from the ברייתא: (1) חוקקין להשלים is a real view (ר' מאיר). (2) ר' מאיר retracted from garden gates. (3) The חכמים support רב דימי: a מקום פטור may be used by either side, but not as a bridge for passing objects between two restricted domains.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב דימי's rule that a מקום פטור cannot be used to transfer between two restricted domains is an important practical principle in the laws of carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: And you learn from (the view of) the Rabbis
that Rav Dimi's ruling is correct,
for when Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael)
he said (that) Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: a place that is not four by four —
it is permitted for the people of the public domain
and for the people of the private domain
to adjust (their loads on their shoulders) on it,
as long as they do not exchange (objects).
phrases.notes: This is the part the חכמים support: a מקום פטור may not be used to move things between two restricted domains.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן אִיתָא לִדְרַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final lesson announced in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's ruling in the name of ר' יוחנן that people may not exchange objects through a מקום פטור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים in the ברייתא, who treat the lock as a מקום פטור but still do not allow it to serve as a bridge between the כרמלית threshold and the רשות היחיד window
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מקום פטור may be used by either side, but not to transfer objects from one restricted domain to another.

steps.title: A bolt with a knob: רבי אליעזר forbids, רבי יוסי permits
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a dispute about locking a door on שבת with a bolt that has a thick knob on its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A bolt that has a knob on its end: רבי אליעזר forbids using it, and רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a disagreement about whether you may lock a door on שבת with a bolt that has a knob at its tip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain bolt shoved into a door frame can look like building (בונה), because it acts like part of the structure. The knob makes the bolt look more like a tool (כלי), since it could also be used to pound things. רבי יוסי treats it as a כלי, so using it is permitted. רבי אליעזר does not, so using it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A bolt or bar used to lock a door
A thick knob at the end of the bolt, which makes it look like a tool

steps.whyThisMatters: The question underneath is whether locking with this bolt counts as using a tool or as building. Everything that follows depends on that.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A bolt that has a knob at its end,
Rabbi Eliezer forbids [using it],
and Rabbi Yosei permits [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶגֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ גְּלוֹסְטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It is unrelated to the earlier discussion of מקום פטור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר forbids locking with a knobbed bolt on שבת, and רבי יוסי permits it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's story: the custom was to permit, and the Elders forbade it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר supports his view with a story about the synagogue in טבריה, where רבן גמליאל and the זקנים forbade a lenient custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: There was an incident in the synagogue in טבריה. People there used to treat this bolt as permitted, until רבן גמליאל and the Elders came and forbade it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings a real-life story to back up his ruling. In his telling, the great Sages stepped in to stop people from using this bolt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing that רבן גמליאל and the זקנים actively forbade a local practice is strong support for רבי אליעזר's strict view. The custom was lenient, and the Sages corrected it to strict.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident, used as proof
They were accustomed to treat it as permitted
רבן גמליאל and the Elders, the leading Sages

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
There was an incident in the synagogue in Tiberias
where they were accustomed to treat it as permitted,
until Rabban Gamliel and the Elders came
and forbade it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּכְנֶסֶת שֶׁבִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an incident to support רבי אליעזר's strict ruling from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the knobbed bolt is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident in the טבריה synagogue, where רבן גמליאל and the זקנים forbade the lenient custom.

steps.title: רבי יוסי tells the story the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the custom in טבריה was actually strict, and רבן גמליאל and the זקנים came and permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: They were accustomed to treat it as forbidden, and רבן גמליאל and the Elders came and permitted it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי does not deny that the story happened. He says it went the other way, so the story actually supports his lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both Sages agree there was a ruling by רבן גמליאל in that synagogue. They disagree only about which direction the ruling went. This cancels רבי אליעזר's proof and turns the same incident into support for permitting the bolt.

keyTerms.meaning: They were accustomed to treat it as forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: There are not two different stories here. It is the same incident, with each Sage remembering the opposite before-and-after.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
They were accustomed to treat it as forbidden,
and Rabban Gamliel and the Elders came
and permitted it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִיסּוּר נָהֲגוּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's version of the incident and reverses it in favor of רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The factual version of the story given by רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The custom was originally strict, not lenient, so רבן גמליאל's ruling was a leniency.

steps.title: גמרא narrows the dispute: everyone agrees if the bolt can be lifted by its rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that if the bolt is tied to the door with a rope strong enough to lift it, all agree it is permitted. It then begins to say where they really disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If the bolt can be lifted by its rope, everyone agrees [that it is permitted]. Where they disagree is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts defining exactly which case the משנה is arguing about. It first rules out one case where there is no argument at all, and then sets up the next move: telling us the case where they do argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the bolt is tied to the door with a rope strong enough to carry it, it is clearly attached to the door, like a part of the door. Locking with it is then simply closing a door, and no one forbids that. So the dispute must be about a weaker or different setup, which the גמרא will identify next.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be lifted by its rope, meaning it is tied to the door strongly enough to hang from it
Where they do argue is... (introduces the real case of the dispute)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic move of narrowing a מחלוקת. Before analyzing a dispute, the גמרא first rules out the cases where there is no argument at all.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Where it can be lifted by its rope,
everyone agrees [that it is permitted].
Where they disagree is...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִיטָּל בְּאִגְדּוֹ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה by narrowing the case in which רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bolt that can be lifted by the rope tying it to the door is permitted according to everyone. The dispute is limited to a different case, introduced by כי פליגי.
